prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Offshore wind farm O&M concept. Boundary: offshore assets, marine/shore facilities, personnel, external orgs; electrical up to Grid Interface Relay. Out of scope: public grid beyond connection, non-farm port ops. Architecture separates offshore equipment, operational services, shore decision functions; defined interface responsibilities; supervisory distinct from planning/human coordination; defined handoffs keep dispatch, marine judgment, work supervision, stores control accountable. Turbine: Turbine Controller (alias Glassfin; produces Pitch Deviation Notice), Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet, Nacelle Condition Monitor, Turbine Sensor Bus. Blade Inspection Drone. Offshore Substation (Morrowick): Main Transformer, Export Cable Monitor. SCADA Gateway (Juniper Vale): supervisory comms offshore↔shore within its control scope. Shore Control Room (Amber Quay): oversight, shore coordination. Maintenance Planning Engine (Thistle Crown): supports Duty Planner. Fleet Dispatch Console (Sable Orchard): vessel assignment/dispatch view for Marine Coordinator. Vessels: Crew Transfer Vessel (Kestrel Bay; personnel/tools), Daughter Craft, Service Operations Vessel; Helideck; Vessel AIS Receiver (produces Position Quality Flag on failed integrity/low confidence). Personnel Tracking Console, North/South Access Scanners. Warehouse System (Mosslight; stock, kits), Spares Hub. Metocean Buoy (Copper Finch): measures wind, waves, current, air temp, pressure; logger timestamps, keeps local history during comms loss; sensors hardened; time sync/health checked. Cybersecurity Gateway (Quiet Harbor): boundary shore services↔offshore networks; only approved protocols/destinations/service accounts; deny-by-default external connectivity; individual authenticated RBAC admin; privileged sessions time-limited, logged, reviewed; protected security logs; segmentation; on boundary loss remote admin restricted, local protection never bypassed. Enabling: Work Permit Portal, comms, fire protection, backup power. Actors: SCADA/Control Engineers, Duty Planner, Field Supervisor (offshore execution, informs Duty Planner), HSE Officer (verifies safety controls/responsibilities), Marine Coordinator, Vessel Master (navigation/safety/transfer go/no-go), Weather Analyst (reviews forecasts/limitations, advises Marine Coordinator), Cybersecurity Analyst (monitors gateway events), Storekeeper, Port Agent, technicians. External: Weather Service (Pale Lantern; Squall Window Bulletin; uses validated observations), grid ops, port, suppliers, emergency response. Requirements: humans retain safety/engineering judgment;

New part:
S121: Interfaces are tested after configuration changes to confirm that permitted functions remain available and prohibited paths remain blocked.
S122: Operational procedures identify the authority for approving access, responding to alarms, and returning affected services to normal operation.
S123: This section describes turbine control and remote observation during offshore operations.
S124: Vessel AIS Receiver is designated Blue Granite for this operational concept.
S125: Blade Inspection Drone is designated Larkspur for this operational concept.
S126: Duty Planner prepares the Transfer Manifest Addendum to capture approved vessel deployment changes.
S127: Glassfin adjusts turbine output within approved operating limits and blocks commands that conflict with active protection conditions.
S128: Pale Lantern issues forecast updates that support timing decisions for remote observation and field work.
S129: Turbine Controller executes authorized control actions and reports its operating state through established control interfaces.
S130: Pitch System changes blade angle in response to turbine control commands and local protection logic.
S131: Converter Cabinet manages electrical conversion while observing equipment limits and protective interlocks.
S132: Nacelle Condition Monitor provides equipment measurements for ongoing assessment of turbine health.
S133: SCADA Gateway presents turbine status and control availability to authorized shore personnel.
S134: Shore Control Room provides a staffed location for supervisory control and operational review.
S135: Control Engineer reviews alarms and operating conditions before issuing a remote command.
S136: Remote commands are subject to role-based authorization and are recorded for later operational review.
S137: Local protection functions retain priority when remote requests conflict with safe operating limits.
S138: Control availability is checked before remote operation begins and after relevant configuration changes.
S139: Vessel AIS Receiver collects vessel position broadcasts to support marine traffic awareness.
S140: The receiver maintains a time-stamped view of nearby vessel movements when broadcast coverage is available.
S141: Marine Coordinator uses the available traffic picture to support coordination of offshore movements.
S142: Blade Inspection Drone captures close-range visual observations of accessible blade surfaces.
S143: Blade Specialist plans inspection passes to provide consistent coverage of areas selected for examination.
S144: Captured imagery is reviewed for visible surface changes and potential maintenance concerns.
S145: Field Supervisor considers remote observations alongside site conditions before recommending follow-up work.
S146: Drone operation is suspended when weather, visibility, or equipment status makes flight unsafe.
S147: Remote observations supplement field assessment and do not replace required physical inspections.
S148: Maintenance Planning Engine can use reviewed condition information when prioritizing future maintenance activities.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
